identity.title: Premiere Night
identity.prompt: Design a video platform that accepts large creator uploads, finishes processing before the premiere, starts playback quickly for a global audience, and stays within budget.

narrative.hook: A major creator's 4K video premieres at 8:00 PM and hundreds of thousands of viewers press Play together.
narrative.stakes: Keep uploads responsive, make accepted videos ready on time, start playback quickly, and control monthly infrastructure cost.
briefingBeats: Synchronous video processing can exhaust user-facing Service capacity before upload returns.
A Queue buffers accepted work, while Workers provide the processing capacity and must be scaled independently.
Object Storage holds large source and rendition bytes; Postgres owns metadata and processing state.
A CDN can absorb popular immutable playback content before it reaches origin infrastructure.
A Queue buys time but cannot compensate for insufficient Worker throughput; cost remains a real constraint.

components.whyHere: Challenge-owned upload and premiere demand enters through this source.
commonMistakes: Treating it as a priced server
components.placementIntent: Start of the user request path

components.whyHere: Global API users may need geography-aware routing.
cons: Does not process media or replace a CDN
commonMistakes: Expecting routing to drain a queue

components.whyHere: Distributes intake and metadata requests across Service capacity.
commonMistakes: Adding Services instead of Workers for backlog

components.whyHere: Handles upload intake, metadata, status, and playback authorization.
commonMistakes: Making the Service process every video inline
components.placementIntent: On the API path, with separate async and object paths

components.whyHere: Popular immutable renditions are excellent edge-cache candidates during the premiere.
pros: Reduces origin reads and startup pressure
cons: Does not help upload or processing
commonMistakes: Putting it behind the Service or using it as storage

components.whyHere: Optional cache for hot metadata, status, or manifests.
cons: Does not store or deliver large media
commonMistakes: Using Redis as a CDN or object store
components.placementIntent: Beside metadata reads, only where graph semantics support it

components.whyHere: Authoritative store for video metadata, creator records, object pointers, and processing state.
cons: Large video bytes are a poor fit
commonMistakes: Storing the 1 GB source in Postgres

components.whyHere: Durably stores source videos, renditions, and thumbnails as large objects.
pros: Separates blob capacity from relational metadata
cons: Origin reads still saturate without CDN offload
components.placementIntent: Upload and Worker output path; playback origin

components.whyHere: Buffers accepted processing work so upload requests do not wait for codecs.
pros: Protects API latency and exposes backlog
cons: Finite capacity and no processing power
commonMistakes: Believing a larger queue fixes a permanent capacity deficit

components.whyHere: Consumes queued work, reads sources, and writes processed outputs.
cons: Idle capacity costs money and cannot deliver playback
commonMistakes: Adding Services instead of processing consumers
components.placementIntent: Consumer of Queue with Object Storage access

object_store.note: Large source and rendition bytes belong in object storage.

async_buffer.note: A queue protects intake but never performs work.

async_consumer.note: Workers turn queued processing units into outputs.

edge_cache.note: Premiere media is highly reusable at the edge.

bands.notes: Backlog reveals whether arrival exceeds drain.
Source and output bytes use object storage.
Popular premiere content should be edge-friendly.
Metadata traffic is much smaller than media bytes.

firstRunExpectation.summary: The inherited Service, Postgres, and Object Storage MVP can accept API traffic but has no asynchronous drain or premiere edge path, so processing deadline and playback startup fail.

playtestChecklist: Synchronous MVP accepts requests but has no processing consumer.
Queue without enough Workers grows backlog while uploads stay responsive.
More Services improve intake but do not drain queued work.
More Workers reduce processing backlog but do not improve playback startup.
Object Storage holds blobs while Postgres remains metadata-only.
CDN on the premiere path reduces origin reads and startup pressure.
Redis helps optional metadata but is not media delivery.
Origin-only playback exposes Object Storage capacity and latency.
A large Queue buys time but cannot overcome arrival above drain capacity.
Overbuilt Workers, storage, or CDN can pass technically while failing budget.
